t.1.96.2: Seeing that his brother Vicitravīrya, the foremost of the wise, had reached young manhood, Bhīṣma set his mind on his marriage.
t.1.96.1: When Citrāṅgada had been slain and his brother was still a boy, O sinless one, Bhīṣma governed that kingdom, abiding by the counsel of Satyavatī.
t.1.96.3: Then, O king, Bhīṣma heard that the three daughters of the lord of Kāśi, equal to Apsarases, were together choosing a husband at a svayaṃvara.
t.1.96.4: Then he, the best of chariot-warriors, clad in armour, went on a single chariot toward the city of Vārāṇasī with his mother's consent.
t.1.96.5: There Bhīṣma, the son of Śaṃtanu, saw the kings assembled together, who had come from every side, and he saw those maidens as well.
t.1.96.6: Then, while the names of the kings were being proclaimed by the thousands, the mighty Bhīṣma himself, O king, chose those maidens.
t.1.96.7: And having placed those maidens upon his chariot, O king, Bhīṣma, best of warriors, spoke to the kings in a voice like the rumbling of a rain-cloud.
t.1.96.8: The wise have declared that daughters should be given to men of virtue after inviting them, adorning the maidens as best one can and bestowing wealth as well.
t.1.96.9: Others give away a maiden in exchange for a pair of cows, others for an agreed sum of wealth; some take her by force, and others after winning her consent.
t.1.96.11: Kṣatriyas praise the svayaṃvara and take part in it, but those who speak on dharma declare that a bride carried off by force is superior.
t.1.96.10: Some approach a maiden who is heedless, and others win her by themselves; know, then, that this is the eighth form of marriage, as handed down by the poets.
t.1.96.12: These maidens, O protectors of the earth, I intend to carry off from here by force; strive then to the utmost of your strength, for victory or for its opposite. I stand here, O protectors of the earth, resolved upon battle.
t.1.96.13: Having thus spoken to the kings and to the king of Kāśi, the mighty Kauravya placed all the maidens upon his own chariot. And having bidden them farewell, he swiftly departed, taking those maidens with him.
t.1.96.14: Then all those kings rose up in fury, touching their own arms and biting their lips.
t.1.96.15: As they hastily and quickly cast off their ornaments and put on their armor, a very great commotion arose among them.
t.1.96.16: O Janamejaya, on every side there was a clashing together of bright ornaments and of armour, like a falling together of stars.
t.1.96.18: Mounting splendid chariots made ready by their charioteers, with fine horses yoked and poised at the pole, those heroes, equipped with every kind of weapon and with weapons raised, pursued the lone Kauravya as he went away.
t.1.96.17: Quickly, here and there, they appeared with their armor and their gleaming ornaments, their brows knit crooked with wrath and indignation, and their eyes likewise reddened.
t.1.96.19: Then, O Bhārata, there arose a battle between them and him, between the one and the many, tumultuous and hair-raising.
t.1.96.20: But they hurled ten thousand arrows at him all at once, and Bhīṣma then swiftly cut them all down before they could reach him.
t.1.96.21: Then all those kings surrounded him on every side and rained a shower of arrows upon him, as rain clouds pour their rain upon a mountain.
t.1.96.22: Having warded off that shower of arrows on every side with his own shafts, he then pierced all the kings in return, each with three arrows.
t.1.96.24: Having vanquished them in battle, the Bhārata, skilled in all weapons, set out with the maidens toward the Bhāratas.
t.1.96.25: Then, O king, the lord of the Śālvas, a great chariot-warrior of immeasurable spirit, struck him, Bhīṣma Śāṃtanava, from behind in battle.
t.1.96.23: Even his enemies praised his swiftness, which surpassed that of all other chariot-borne warriors, and the way he protected himself in battle.
t.1.96.27: "Stop, stop, you lecher!" so said to Bhīṣma that king, the mighty-armed lord of the Śālvas, driven on by indignation.
t.1.96.28: Then Bhīṣma, that tiger among men, crusher of enemy hosts, stirred by those words, blazed with anger like a smokeless fire.
t.1.96.26: He was like a rival herd-leader, best of the mighty, who has followed a female elephant in heat and strikes another elephant on the hindquarters with his two tusks.
t.1.96.29: Taking his stand on the law of the warrior, free from fear and agitation, the great chariot-warrior turned his chariot back toward Śālva.
t.1.96.30: Seeing him turning back, all those kings became mere spectators at the encounter between Bhīṣma and Śālva.
t.1.96.32: Then the king of the Śālvas, best of men, showered Bhīṣma, the son of Śaṃtanu, with arrows, swift-flying shafts by the hundreds of thousands.
t.1.96.31: Roaring like two bulls contending over a cow in heat, those two mighty warriors, rich in strength and valor, charged against each other.
t.1.96.33: Having seen Bhīṣma first hard pressed by Śālva, those kings were filled with amazement and cried out, "Well done! Well done!"
t.1.96.34: Seeing his dexterity in battle, all those kings, the lords of men, delighted, honored Śālva with words of praise.
t.1.96.35: Then, having heard the words of the kṣatriyas, Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, conqueror of enemy cities, grew angry and said, "Stop! Stop!"
t.1.96.37: Then the Kaurava properly fitted the Vāruṇa weapon, and with it, O lord of men, he crushed the four horses of the king of the Śālvas.
t.1.96.36: And, enraged, he said to his charioteer: “Drive to where this king stands, so that I may slay him today, as the king of birds slays a serpent.”
t.1.96.38: Warding off the weapons of the king of the Śālvas with his own weapons, that Kaurava Bhīṣma, O tiger among kings, slew his charioteer, and then with a single weapon he slew his excellent horses.
t.1.96.39: For the sake of the maiden, O best of men, Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, having then defeated that best of kings, let him go alive. Then Śālva went to his own city, O bull of the Bharatas.
t.1.96.40: And the kings who had been there, eager to witness the svayaṃvara, they too went back to their own kingdoms, O conqueror of enemy cities.
t.1.96.41: Having thus won those maidens, Bhīṣma, the best of warriors, set out for Hāstinapura, where that Kaurava king was.
t.1.96.43: Unwounded, having destroyed his enemies in battle, the son of the ocean-going river, whose prowess was beyond measure, brought away the daughters of the king of Kāśī.
t.1.96.42: In a very short time, O king, he passed beyond forests and rivers, and mountains covered with many kinds of trees.
t.1.96.44: That righteous one took them as if they were daughters-in-law, as if younger sisters, and as if daughters, and went to the Kurus.
t.1.96.45: Bhīṣma, the brother, gave all of them, endowed with virtues and won by valor, to his younger brother Vicitravīrya.
t.1.96.46: Having accomplished, by the law of the good, a deed beyond human power, the self-possessed knower of dharma, after privately reaching a decision together with Satyavatī, set about the marriage of his brother Vicitravīrya.
t.1.96.49: At that svayaṃvara, Śālva was the one I was to choose as my husband. Knowing this, O knower of dharma, act then in accordance with dharma.
t.1.96.47: Then, as Bhīṣma was about to have the marriage performed, the eldest of them, the daughter of the lord of Kāśi, a virtuous woman, spoke these words to him.
t.1.96.48: The lord of Saubha was long ago chosen by me in my heart as my husband, and I too was chosen by him before; and this was also the wish of my father.
t.1.96.50: Thus addressed by that maiden in the assembly of brahmins, the heroic Bhīṣma fell to reflection fitting for that very matter.
t.1.96.52: Bhīṣma gave Ambikā and Ambālikā as wives to his younger brother Vicitravīrya, with the rite prescribed by the ordinance.
t.1.96.51: Then he, the knower of dharma, having reached a decision with brahmins who had mastered the Vedas, gave leave to Ambā, the eldest daughter of the lord of Kāśi.
t.1.96.53: Having taken the hand of those two, Vicitravīrya, righteous in spirit yet proud of his beauty and youth, became given over to desire.
t.1.96.55: Once it was settled that they had gained a husband worthy of themselves, the two of them honored the noble Vicitravīrya.
t.1.96.54: And those two as well, tall and dark-complexioned, with dark curling hair, endowed with red and prominent nails, with full hips and breasts…
t.1.96.56: And he, resembling the Aśvins in beauty and possessing the strength and valor of a god, became the one who stirred the hearts of all women.
t.1.96.57: Having sported with those two for seven years, the lord of the earth, Vicitravīrya, still young, fell ill with consumption.
t.1.96.59: Abiding by the counsel of Satyavatī, Bhīṣma, accompanied by the officiating priests and all the bulls among the Kurus, had all the funeral rites of King Vicitravīrya duly performed.
t.1.96.58: Even as his friends strove together with trusted physicians, the Kauravya went to the abode of Yama, like the sun going to its setting.
